text:
Anton Lundell scored three times, two of them in the last ten minutes of the third period, and Florida pulled away from a Winnipeg team that is now winless in eight (0-6-2). The Jets had cut it to 3-2 on Morgan Barron's goal at 8:46, but Lundell answered at 13:33 and again at 18:21. He was drafted 12th overall in 2020 out of HIFK in Finland, and on a night he finished with eight shots on goal, this was the payoff.

Our numbers say the result was fair. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count, favored Florida 4.66 to 2.49, and Florida would win about 75 percent of simulated replays of this game. Winnipeg made its best push in the second period, out-chancing the Panthers 1.78 to 0.77 and getting a power-play goal from Kyle Connor. Then the third period belonged to Florida, 2.87 expected goals to 0.27. The Panthers also took 69 shot attempts to 48 and won 37 of 59 faceoffs.

Seth Jones had a goal and two assists, and Sam Reinhart added a goal and an assist, including the power-play opener late in the first. Akira Schmid made 22 saves, close to what the chances called for, and Nico Daws was just as even-keeled in a 4-on-37 night he couldn't do much about. Florida has won three straight and beat the Jets 5-1 in their meeting on Oct. 27. Winnipeg's skid has now reached eight games, and the team has little to show from either meeting.
